translations.text: The elder writes to the beloved Gaius, whom I love in truth.
My beloved, I pray that you may prosper in everything and be in good health, just as your soul prospers.
I was very glad when the brothers came and testified about your faithfulness to the truth, just as you yourself live by the truth.
For I have no greater joy than this: to hear that my children walk in truth.
My beloved, you are acting faithfully in whatever you do for the brothers, even for strangers.
They have testified to your love before the church. You will do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God.
For they went out for the sake of the Name, taking nothing from the Gentiles.
We therefore ought to welcome such people, so that we may become fellow workers for the truth.
You wrote something [?] to the church, because Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, does not welcome us.

Therefore, if I come, I will remind you of the things he does, speaking malicious nonsense against us. And he is not content with this: he himself does not welcome the brothers, and he prevents those who welcome them and throws them out of the church.
My beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. Whoever does good is from God. Whoever does evil has not seen God.
Everyone has testified on behalf of Demetrius, and so has the truth. We too also testify, and you yourself know that our testimony is true.
I have many things to write to you, but I do not want to write them to you with ink and a reed pen.
But I hope to see you soon, and we will speak with one another face to face.
May peace be with you. Our friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.
